q: last night I was reading about other people’s experiences of pregnancy rage and so many of them said things along the line of “he’s still such an angel, and he’s so helpful, and he cooks and he does so much for me”. I realised that my husband doesn’t do anything for me.
cx: At 12+5, reading other women's posts makes her see her irritation differently.

q: When I haven’t been able to stomach food, I still cook him nutritious meals. It’s totally taken for granted.
cx: Same woman on the housework she still carries.

q: I bought myself a Polaroid camera to take weekly bump photos and haven’t event taken one yet.
cx: At 8 weeks, tired and not feeling like herself, the bump-photo plan untouched.

q: I envisioned this pregnancy to bring my and my husband together but I’m so out of it.
cx: Same woman on how the pregnancy is not what she imagined.

q: It’s to the point now where I dread bedtime, I’d rather not try to sleep and just stay awake forever.
cx: At almost 27 weeks, restless legs keep her up until 4–5am each night.

q: I take magnesium gummies, I stretch, I massage my legs (via husband, me, and massage gun). I’ve tried unisom to knock me out
cx: Same woman lists what she has tried.

q: it's all over my face so I am so far from having a pregnancy glow that I'm losing the will to leave the house.
cx: UK woman at 8 weeks, a lifelong skin condition flaring before her booking appointment.

q: the rest of the time I feel like I’m going to be trapped in school schedules and baby schedules and I’m losing the remainder of my 20s where I could be partying and meeting people etc.
cx: UK woman, 26, newly pregnant earlier than planned, mourning her travel plans.

q: I recently told my husband that I would appreciate a push present. He was like "that seems expensive" and "don't you get a baby for pushing"
cx: A non-native-English poster on asking for a push present.

q: I just wanted something small to keep me occupied during the post-partum-period. Maybe a coloring set or a cross stitch kit, maybe even something that I could make a baby-item out of
cx: Same woman on what she actually wanted.

q: But low and behold, the best husband ever just bought me a 900€ flute.
cx: Same woman: her husband's gift, which he didn't see as a push present.

q: "since you had to give up carbs, I thought you might want this as a little pick-me-up. You said that pregnancy has been hard on you and I wanted to say thank you for enduring it"
cx: Same woman quoting her husband's reason for the gift.

q: I don’t understand the pattern, the timings, nothing. Sometimes after eating, sometimes before. Please give me a guide. I can’t be living like this and just feeling like this all the time.
cx: At 6 weeks, unable to tell nausea from gas, she asks strangers for a guide.

q: we’re out of town for my husbands family thing and I’m expected to be out all day. I’m exhausted. [...] sometimes I don’t think my husband really understands how exhausting it can be.
cx: At 25 weeks, away at her husband's family event.

q: I am crying looking at old photos. I am afraid I will never look like that again in my life.
cx: A first-timer at 30 weeks missing her old body.

q: I am afraid of giving birth and all of the responsibilities… I am really excited at the same time and somehow feeling guilty for thinking this way as I am supposed to be excited the whole time
cx: Same woman on fear of birth mixed with guilt for not being only excited.

q: It is so difficult and confusing.. that I am not able to workout. The way I roll out of bed, the size of my nose !!
cx: Same woman listing the changes.

q: I feel like my daughter has two adults in the house, but only one actual parent.
cx: At 12 weeks with a 15-month-old, a mother on a husband who barely parents.
r: past pregnancy loss mentioned elsewhere in post

q: All of this makes me terrified of how much harder it will be to protect and solo-parent two children while going through postpartum again. The first time I feel like I barely survived.
cx: Same mother dreading a second postpartum without real help.
r: past pregnancy loss mentioned elsewhere in post

q: I mentioned getting help at the beginning of the year well before I was pregnant again and his response was something like "there’s no reason to pay someone to come when you’re home five days."
cx: Same mother on raising paid help with her husband.
r: past pregnancy loss mentioned elsewhere in post

q: I probably have enough in my personal account to pay for a few months of help, but I would still have to get him on board.
cx: Same mother: she could pay for help, but needs him to agree.
r: past pregnancy loss mentioned elsewhere in post

q: Is it crazy to still have my wedding 5 months postpartum? I know I probably won't be able to get my dress until very close to the wedding. I guess I'm just worried about how I'll feel about myself.
cx: Newly pregnant with her second, due in May; dream venue for October already paid in full.

q: All I want to do is read reddit posts with baby tips and watch Instagram videos of pelvic floor exercises (and then not really do any of them).
cx: At 5 weeks, foggy and reading everything about babies and birth.

q: I wonder if my confidence in its success is only inspiring me further to waste time reading birthing and baby tips!
cx: Same woman on why she keeps reading birth tips so early.

q: managing a house, a yard, eating nutritiously for the baby, plus work by myself has felt impossible. I have the means to do this alone financially but I don’t have the means to hire people to help me.
cx: At 22 weeks, 35 and first-time, her boyfriend left at 11 weeks; she has just stepped up to senior manager.

q: He really hasn’t been around at all in what feels like months now beyond coming to ultrasound appointments. I have a follow up anatomy scan this Friday and I really don’t know if he intends to come or not.
cx: Same woman on the absent father and the upcoming scan.

q: I knew taking a new job was a risk but I frankly was ignorant about how much my mental state would change while being pregnant.
cx: Same woman on taking a bigger job while pregnant.

q: I am in Canada, so I am entitled to 12/18mths mat leave with a reduced income. However, I want to go back to working early so I can get my car paid off instead of surrendering it.
cx: At 38 weeks with a planned section, planning to return to work at 2–3 months.

q: My problem is I don’t have a village, but I do have my mom here for a short period, and I haven’t got a daycare yet.
cx: Same woman on help after the birth.
